sections.heading: 1. Operator and scope
paragraphs: PLUG is operated by Abubakar Bolakale in the United States. Contact privacy@plugapp.com about these terms, privacy, or an account concern. These starter terms are a review draft for invited private testing, not a public-launch agreement. Merely viewing this draft does not accept a new agreement. A dated final version must be presented clearly with affirmative acceptance before it replaces the existing onboarding notice.

sections.heading: 2. Eligibility and safety
paragraphs: The intended minimum age is 15. A person aged 15 to 17 needs a parent or legal guardian’s permission and any additional safeguards required by applicable law. The current test app has no completed age or parental-permission process; minors must not be enrolled until those safeguards are in place. Do not misrepresent your age or authority. PLUG is not an emergency service; contact the appropriate local emergency service when needed.

sections.heading: 3. What the test service does
paragraphs: Current testing covers Google and guest access, account sessions, consent records, and limited interface/API testing. Apple sign-in and real SMS delivery are deferred. Booking, supplier outreach, purchases, payments, Scout contributions and AI fulfillment are not currently offered. A successful API response or a prototype screen is not a reservation, order, supplier acceptance or promise of availability.

sections.heading: 4. Test access and accounts
paragraphs: Use your own authorized sign-in account, keep your device secure and report suspected misuse. PLUG does not ask you to disclose your provider password or one-time codes to support. Guests receive limited access. Creating a new account through the supported guest-upgrade flow can preserve that guest identity; signing into an existing account switches accounts and does not merge guest activity. Do not rely on a guest account as your sole record of important information.

sections.heading: 5. Acceptable use
paragraphs: Do not use PLUG for fraud, harassment, impersonation, unlawful content, unauthorized access, attempts to obtain another person’s data, or disruption of the service. Do not bypass access controls or rate limits. Security testing requires an agreed scope; if you discover a vulnerability, report it privately and avoid accessing or retaining other people’s information. Nothing here prohibits lawful consumer reviews, reporting to regulators, protected disclosures or conduct that applicable law permits.

sections.heading: 6. Content and feedback
paragraphs: You retain ownership of material you submit. You must have permission to provide it. You grant PLUG only the nonexclusive permission needed to receive, process, store and display that material to operate, secure and support the test service, subject to the Privacy Policy and applicable law. This is not permission to sell your content, advertise with your identity or train unrelated AI models. Voluntary product feedback may be used to improve PLUG without payment or an obligation to implement it; this does not transfer your unrelated intellectual property or permit disclosure of personal information contrary to the Privacy Policy.

sections.heading: 7. PLUG intellectual property
paragraphs: PLUG and its licensors retain their rights in the app, branding and original materials. You receive a limited, nonexclusive, revocable right to use the authorized test build for its intended purpose. Open-source components remain subject to their own licenses. No restriction overrides rights you have under applicable law or an applicable open-source license.

sections.heading: 8. Fees and third-party services
paragraphs: PLUG does not charge a service fee in this private test. Your mobile carrier or internet provider may charge for connectivity. These terms do not authorize future purchases, subscriptions or automatic renewals. Any later paid service requires its own clear terms and affirmative authorization. Google, Apple and other third-party services have their own terms and privacy notices; PLUG does not control their availability and does not disclaim its own legal obligations by using them.

sections.heading: 9. Availability and changes
paragraphs: This is development software. Features may be interrupted, changed or withdrawn, and test records may be lost. Keep independent copies of information that matters to you. We do not promise uninterrupted access, accurate prototype results or suitability for critical decisions. Changes to personal-information use remain subject to the Privacy Policy and applicable law; test status does not permit arbitrary use of your information.

sections.heading: 10. Suspension, ending use and deletion
paragraphs: You may stop using PLUG at any time. Access may be restricted to protect the service, investigate misuse or meet legal obligations. Where appropriate and lawful, we will explain the restriction and provide a way to contact us. Signing out or uninstalling does not delete server records. Contact privacy@plugapp.com for an account or deletion request. The current internal deletion action revokes sessions and marks the account deleted; it is not full erasure, and no in-app deletion screen is available yet. Mandatory privacy rights continue after access ends.

sections.heading: 11. Warranty disclaimer
paragraphs: To the extent applicable law permits, the private test is provided “as is” and “as available,” without implied warranties of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose or non-infringement. This disclaimer does not remove express commitments we make or any warranty, remedy or consumer protection that cannot lawfully be excluded. It does not promise immunity from claims.

sections.heading: 12. Liability limits
paragraphs: To the extent permitted by applicable law, PLUG is not liable for indirect or consequential losses caused by use of the private test, such as lost profits or business opportunities. Whether a loss is direct or indirect depends on applicable law and the circumstances, not just this label. Nothing excludes or limits liability for fraud, intentional misconduct, gross negligence, injury or death caused by negligence where such limits are prohibited, unlawful handling of personal information where liability cannot be excluded, or any other non-waivable liability. No blanket release of all claims or zero-dollar liability cap is imposed by this draft.

sections.heading: 13. Concerns and disputes
paragraphs: Please contact privacy@plugapp.com with a description of a concern so we can try to resolve it. Contacting us first is voluntary and does not suspend a filing deadline or prevent urgent relief, a regulator complaint, small-claims proceedings or another lawful remedy. This starter draft does not impose mandatory arbitration, a class-action waiver, a shortened limitation period or an exclusive court location. Applicable law and any non-waivable consumer protections govern; a state-specific clause requires review once the operator’s legal location is confirmed.

sections.heading: 14. Updates and general terms
paragraphs: Material changes must be communicated appropriately and require renewed acceptance when necessary. Do not treat continued use alone as acceptance of a materially different agreement without the legally required notice and choice. If a provision cannot be enforced, the remaining lawful provisions continue to the extent permitted. Failure to enforce a provision once is not a waiver of future rights. These terms do not create an employment, partnership or agency relationship. The Privacy Policy explains data practices; acknowledging it is not blanket consent to unrelated processing.

sections.heading: 1. Operator and current scope
paragraphs: Abubakar Bolakale operates PLUG in the United States. Contact privacy@plugapp.com. This September 30, 2026 draft describes the private test, not all roadmap features. Google and guest access are available. Apple sign-in and real SMS delivery are deferred. Booking, supplier outreach, payments, photos, push notifications and AI fulfillment are not yet live.

sections.heading: 2. Information processed
paragraphs: PLUG processes provider authentication credentials and identity claims, a keyed hash of the verified provider identifier, internal user identifiers, account status, session records, consent versions and timestamps. The current account database has no name or email profile fields; transient authentication claims can contain information not stored in that profile. Guest identifiers and hashed identifiers can still be personal information. PLUG does not receive your Google password. App session credentials are stored in the iPhone Keychain; the server stores hashes of PLUG session credentials.

sections.heading: 3. Requests and technical records
paragraphs: The test request API can receive submitted text and coordinates, including precise coordinates; it validates and acknowledges requests without arranging a booking. Support receives information you choose to send. Request IDs, outcomes, security events and some network-address prefixes support troubleshooting and abuse prevention. Connection providers process technical metadata, including IP addresses. Do not submit unnecessary sensitive information, another person’s private information, passwords or one-time codes.

sections.heading: 4. Purposes and recipients
paragraphs: Information is used to authenticate accounts, maintain and revoke sessions, record notice acknowledgments, prevent misuse, diagnose problems and answer support or privacy requests. Information may also be used for an applicable legal obligation or a legitimate legal claim. Google processes Google sign-in. Cloudflare carries public test traffic to team-controlled development infrastructure. Authorized team members and the inbox provider may process information needed for operation or support. Apple and Twilio would process authentication or delivery data only when their integrations are enabled. We do not sell personal information or use it for cross-context behavioral advertising in the current test; no production AWS, AI, analytics or maps processing is claimed.

sections.heading: 5. Retention and deletion
paragraphs: Test database records remain until removed through an authorized process. An automated record-deletion and backup-expiry schedule has not been established. Access credentials expire after 15 minutes; refresh credentials expire after 30 days for a verified account or 7 days for a guest. Credential expiry does not erase database records. Internal account deletion revokes sessions and marks an account deleted, but is not complete personal-data erasure. Audit records are append-only. Retention limits and a verified deletion/backup process must be implemented before public launch; no arbitrary deletion deadline is promised here.

sections.heading: 6. Requests, rights and security
paragraphs: Contact privacy@plugapp.com to request access, correction or deletion, or raise a concern. We may need proportionate verification of your identity and any agent’s authority, without collecting passwords or OTPs. Rights and response deadlines depend on applicable law; requests, refusals and any permitted extensions must be handled accordingly. You may contact the relevant regulator, and exercising legal rights must not lead to unlawful discrimination. Signing out, removing the app or withdrawing provider authorization does not itself erase PLUG records. HTTPS, Keychain, hashed credentials, access controls, rotation, replay protection and rate limits reduce risk but cannot guarantee absolute security. Incidents must be assessed and notified as required by law.

sections.heading: 7. Age, location and changes
paragraphs: PLUG’s intended minimum age is 15, with parent or guardian permission for ages 15 to 17. Age and parental-permission safeguards are not implemented, so minors must not be enrolled in this test until those safeguards are ready. Notify us if a child under 15 has supplied information so it can be investigated and handled appropriately. The operator is in the United States; provider processing locations and any required international-transfer measures must be confirmed before offering the service in additional regions. Material changes will be dated and communicated with any legally required choice or consent. Future features require updated disclosures before their data collection begins.

sections.heading: Contact
paragraphs: For account, privacy, security or private-test concerns, email privacy@plugapp.com or contact the person who invited you. This inbox was confirmed by the operator; no 24-hour response or emergency monitoring is promised.

sections.heading: What to include
paragraphs: Describe the issue, approximate time, app version, steps to reproduce and request ID if one is shown. Remove personal notifications from screenshots. Never include passwords, one-time codes, session tokens or provider credentials.

sections.heading: Privacy and account requests
paragraphs: Explain whether you want access, correction, account closure or deletion. We will identify a proportionate verification route. Do not assume signing out or uninstalling deletes server data; the current internal account-deletion action is not full erasure.

sections.heading: Security reports
paragraphs: Report the affected feature and a minimal safe reproduction. Do not access other users’ information, disrupt availability or send stolen data. A report does not authorize further testing; agree any testing scope first.

sections.heading: Emergencies
paragraphs: PLUG is not an emergency service. Contact the appropriate emergency service directly if there is an immediate safety issue.
